summary: Adds a shared security-headers middleware (driven by findings from a new OWASP ZAP scanning pass on mymatasan), replacing the old greet middleware that only set a 'Server: r450k' header. Every response now gets X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Strict-Transport-Security over TLS, and never advertises a Server header/version; this covers every response including auth 401s, rate-limit 429s, static assets, and the setup page, and applies to all three apps (mymatasan, myseliasan, myidsan) since the middleware lives in shared infra/apphost. A new optional 'securityHeaders' config block (separate from the pre-existing encryption-at-rest 'security' block) lets each app tune or disable individual headers and opt in to a Content-Security-Policy; mymatasan's config.json/config.dev.json now ship a tested CSP. To support that CSP (and fix a ZAP subresource-integrity finding), the mymatasan front-end's Quicksand font is now self-hosted (assets/fonts.css + woff2 files) instead of loaded from Google Fonts, removing the app's only cross-origin resource. A new tools/zaproxy/ dev-tooling directory (scan scripts + automation-framework plans) supports repeatable ZAP scans; it is developer tooling only, like tools/tgbridge, with no shipped-app doc coverage.
compatibility: Backward compatible for every existing install: all securityHeaders fields are optional and hardened defaults apply automatically when the block is omitted, matching the previous absence of these headers plus the header hardening itself (net-new protection, no behavior an existing client depended on is removed). Content-Security-Policy remains opt-in and is only sent when explicitly configured (mymatasan's config.json is the only app that sets one so far). The self-hosted font is a drop-in replacement with no visual change. No database migration and no required config changes.
